canonical_definition:
What it is. Across the cited work, Natural Instructions is described as a dataset for evaluating a model's ability to follow natural language instructions across a wide range of tasks. One usage snippet also places it in generation-task testing, where papers report testing method effects on Natural Instructions.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers use Natural Instructions to measure Instruction following. It is linked to one behavioral indicator, Instruction following, and to no constructs, so the available measurement claims converge on that single target rather than being spread across multiple outcomes.

Space of uses. In the available usage evidence, papers position Natural Instructions as a training and evaluation dataset alongside XSum and the WMT-14 en-de translation dataset. Another paper uses it to test generation-task effects of different methods.

relationships.evidence: Our experiments use three datasets for training and evaluation: the XSum summarization dataset (Narayan et al., 2018), the WMT-14 en-de translation dataset (Bojar et al., 2014), and the instruction-following dataset Natural Instructions (Mishra et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2022).
